questions.q: Does TypeScript have separate types for integers and floating-point numbers?
options: Yes, int and float are separate types
No, both are covered by the single number type
Yes, but only for values under 2^53
No, all numeric values must use bigint
questions.explain: TypeScript (following JavaScript) uses one number type for all numeric values, with no separate integer type.

questions.q: What's the difference between number[] and a tuple like [string, number]?
options: There is no difference
number[] allows any number of elements of that type; a tuple fixes both the exact length and the type at each position
Tuples can only hold numbers
number[] is stricter than a tuple
questions.explain: An array type like number[] can be any length, all the same type; a tuple locks in a specific length with a specific type per position.

questions.q: Why do blockchain libraries commonly use bigint instead of number for wei amounts?
options: bigint is required by all blockchains
number can't safely represent integers beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, which wei amounts routinely exceed
bigint runs faster at runtime
number doesn't support arithmetic operations
questions.explain: Wei values (or any 18-decimal token's smallest unit) commonly exceed JavaScript's safe integer range, so bigint is used to avoid precision loss.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between any and unknown?
options: any and unknown behave identically
any disables type checking on that value entirely; unknown still requires you to narrow the type before using it
unknown disables type checking; any requires narrowing
any can only be used with numbers
questions.explain: unknown accepts any value too, but TypeScript won't let you call methods or access properties on it until you've proven what type it actually is — any skips that check entirely.

questions.q: What does the never type describe?
options: A function that returns undefined
A variable that can never be reassigned
A function that never returns at all, because it always throws or loops forever
An array that is always empty
questions.explain: never is used for functions whose control flow never reaches a return — for example, a function that always throws an error.
